verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: yes - the draft covers both asks: the email waits for a complete file, and failed exports become visible. The ACs and the sketch placement still need repair before the gate.
findings:
- [major] other @ "## Idea" (all four paragraphs, from "Start by introducing a completion record" through "single readiness decision shared by the customer page and email sender") - The Idea section must keep exactly one attributed sketch line (SKILL step 4). Here the reporter's sketch fills four paragraphs: a completion record schema, a retry loop, a reconciliation task, a support view, metrics, retention and a rollout switch. Everything after the first line is overflow, but the overflow was neither cut from Idea nor moved into the single permitted comment. The ticket now carries "how" in its body. → Keep only the opening attributed line ("The reporter suggests waiting until the file is complete before sending the email, then making the ready status agree with what the customer can actually download."). Move the remaining Idea text verbatim into the `Reporter note:` comment. The Human input asks to "keep the implementation detail for whoever picks this up", so relocate the text; do not delete it. The same overflow applies to the one-line Idea branch: joining the paragraphs into one physical line does not make them one sketch line, because the sentence count and content are unchanged. — probed: draft.md Idea vs source.md ("reporter supplied ... all four Idea paragraphs ... as a proposed implementation sketch") - sketch retained in the body, not demoted
- [major] gap @ "## Proposed Reporter note" - The note keeps the displaced completion-hook sentence. It is missing the other displaced reporter material: the Idea overflow and the ExportLatch call-order sentence. Only one comment per issue is allowed, so all of it must share this body. → Append the Context ExportLatch sentence and the Idea overflow paragraphs below "move the completion hook to exportReady; the adapter has 240 lines." — probed: draft.md note section - only the hook sentence present
- [major] ambiguity @ "The ExportLatch reads the staging ledger, calls the mail adapter, and only then commits the row counter to the completion store." - This sentence breaks the wording contract twice:
  - It is a reporter-supplied mechanism that the draft states as Context fact. The source calls it part of the sketch.
  - It uses undefined repo jargon (ExportLatch, staging ledger, mail adapter, row counter, completion store), against rule 6.
  - Fix: remove it from Context and move it to the Reporter note. The plain-words sentence before it ("the export email can arrive while the file is still being written") already carries the triage meaning.
  — probed: source.md - "reporter supplied the Context's ExportLatch call-order sentence ... as a proposed implementation sketch"
- [major] not-actionable @ "## Acceptance Criteria" - The rows are not `- [ ]` items, and neither names a setup, action and observable result.
  - "sent only after its CSV file is complete" gives no observable that shows completeness.
  - "show Failed" does not say where.
  - Suggested rows:
    - `- [ ] Given an export whose file is still being written, no export email is sent until the write finishes; the first download from the email contains every expected row`
    - `- [ ] Given an export whose writer fails, the customer's export status shows Failed (not Ready) and no ready email is sent`
  — probed: none
- [minor] other @ "Example: 12 of 20 first downloads were empty." - The source and date are missing. → "Example: support measured 12 of 20 first downloads empty on 2026-10-20." — probed: source.md - "Support measured 12 of 20 empty first downloads on 2026-10-20"
- [minor] other @ "a customer requested a report at noon and saw Ready" - The UI-behavior claim has no evidence provenance, which the evidence gate requires. → Add "(reported to support on 2026-10-20; support confirmed failed exports currently show Ready)", or add evidence: `none (<reason>)`. — probed: source.md - date and support confirmation present, omitted in draft
lean: nothing to cut
